description: Generic reference taxonomy of fault injection classes commonly considered when analyzing small control/datapath modules such as entropy post-processors. This list is provided as background reference material for the analyst; it does not indicate which fault class, if any, is effective against a specific module or signal.

fault_classes.description: A transient perturbation of the clock signal (e.g. an extra narrow pulse, a stretched period, or a dropped edge) intended to cause a flip-flop to sample its input at an unintended time or to skip/duplicate a clock edge.

A brief dip or spike in supply voltage intended to cause setup/hold violations in sequential logic, potentially corrupting register updates on one or more clock edges without affecting the clock tree directly.

An attacker with physical or adjacent access forces a control input to a fixed logic-low level for a sustained window, overriding its normal driver. This is a generic technique applicable to any single-bit control input and can be used to suppress handshake signals, block reset deassertion, or prevent a request line from toggling.

The complementary technique to signal_hold_low: a control input is forced to a fixed logic-high level for a sustained window, overriding its normal driver, potentially causing a request or enable line to appear continuously asserted.

A single stored bit in a register or latch is flipped from its correct value to the opposite value, typically modeling ionizing radiation (SEU) or a localized EM/laser pulse targeting a specific flip-flop cell.
An unintended assertion (or premature deassertion) of the reset signal is induced, causing registers to load their reset-state values outside of the module's intended reset sequencing.
